title: seven positions where a capability-reading coercion member is within reach but does not run record an empty row, compile with no layer at all, and print what ECMAScript says they print
notes: specification/requirements.mdx, 'Inference': 'Calling a function with unsatisfied requirements MUST add those capabilities to the caller's R row.' The obligation is about CALLING. A member that is declared and never invoked adds nothing, and this case is the over-correction guard for the whole coercion family: seven programs in which a Db-reading member sits one token away from a coercion and must still be charged to nobody. The evidence is that the file compiles and RUNS with no layer at all, and that each line prints the value ECMAScript specifies, which is what says the member really did not run rather than that its effect was optimised away. THE ORACLE HERE IS THE RUN TIME, NOT THE COMPILER, and that was measured rather than assumed: `SMITHERS2102` fires on top-level CALLS, and every function here is reached through `main`, which the harness calls — so a wrongly charged row is NOT refused. It aborts. Temporarily making position 1 read the capability for real was checked against both backends and both exit 1, the reference with `Panic: capability 'Db' was not provided` and the fork with `Panic: unsatisfied Context requirement`. That is a stronger observation than a refusal would be, and it is why this case is written as an `output` case rather than as an empty diagnostics set. Each position is a distinct mechanism a fix could break: (1) a Db-reading `valueOf` at a STRING-hint position, where `OrdinaryToPrimitive` calls `toString` first, gets `Object.prototype.toString`, gets a primitive back and stops — the printed `[object Object]` is the proof the walk ended there; (2) a `Symbol.toPrimitive` that shadows BOTH a Db-reading `valueOf` and a Db-reading `toString`, so the exotic member wins and neither of the other two is reachable; (3) and (4) a LOCAL binding spelled `Number` and `String`, called through the same parentheses its ambient sibling case is charged at, which is what forces the ambient rule to key on the binding rather than on the spelling; (5) reading `obj.valueOf` without calling it, which is a property read of a function value; (6) a tagged template, whose substitutions are handed to the tag unconverted — the printed `xobject` is `typeof value`, so the object arrived at the tag as an object and was never coerced; (7) a computed member name whose value is an ordinary string. WHY THESE SEVEN ARE ONE CASE: they fail together under every fix that would break any of them, because the shared cause is one predicate deciding whether a coercion runs, and the corpus is not improved by seven files that differ only in which line of one program they keep. WHAT THIS CASE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT PIN: the `Object.prototype.toString` text as a language promise. `[object Object]` is ECMAScript's, not Smithers's, and it is declared here because it is the observable that discriminates position 1 from a walk that reached `valueOf` — not because the language owns the string. It also does not pin `JSON.stringify`, where both backends currently over-approximate by charging a `toString` that `JSON.stringify` would not call; that is a recorded shared residual and belongs to the lane that settles it. WHY THE MODULE DECLARES ITS OWN `Number` AND `String`: positions 3 and 4 need the shadow at module scope, which means nothing else in the file may use the ambient ones — hence every number is stringified by a template literal rather than by `String(...)`. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: mutating the first declared stdout line from `[object Object]` to `3` — which is exactly what this program prints if the string-hint walk reaches `valueOf`, so the mutation is the real failure mode rather than a nonsense one — turns the case red on BOTH backends with the stdout diff printed, and the expectation was restored byte-identically (sha256 53017d2a45bf22d8cbae8339b876cb9f1315fb2ad76de2c5d2e22e25cdc58195 before and after, that digest being this file's content at the moment the mutation ran — the sentence recording it is appended afterwards, so the shipped file necessarily hashes differently). The paired refusal controls are `every-spelling-of-a-coercion-member-charges-the-same-row`, `a-parenthesised-ambient-coercion-callee-charges-the-same-row` and `a-toString-returning-an-object-falls-through-to-valueOf`: this case is what stops those three from being satisfied by a backend that simply charges everything.
